The core fix holds, and all three round-1 problems are resolved in the code, not only in the ledger:
- Point 1: `halt_all_sync` now calls `_reassert_halt_pause()` (app.py:7692).

- Point 3: `start()` and `_start_lanes()` use `_reassert_halt_pause_soon()`, which runs the re-pause on its own daemon thread, one at a time.

What I checked:
- `_unpause_all` returns early on `_is_halted()`. That one guard covers `stop()`, `pause()`, the between-passes sweep and `_startup_unpause`. The latch is engaged before `_stop_lanes`, and `release_halt` and the fleet release both clear it before `release_for_halt`.
- The other unpause sites run inside a pass (repath reconcile, the accept flow) or check the halt themselves (`borrowed_folders._reconcile_one`, `shared_folders`), so none of them releases a folder under a halt.
- There is one Sequencer construction site, and it wires `halted=lambda: self.halt.active`.

- All 9 tests in `test_halt_holds_lane_c.py` fail against `git show HEAD:` copies of app.py, sync/sequencer.py and sync/repath.py (scratch package; I confirmed `ccsync_companion.__file__` resolved there). Each fails on its own assertion or on the missing `_reassert_halt_pause`.

Two residual defects remain, both minor and both introduced by this fix:

1. Point 2 is fixed for project folders but not for borrowed lender folders.
   - After a restart onto a halted machine, the re-pause now pauses the lender folders it derives from the cached selection (sequencer.py:1130).
   - The release does not bring them back. `release_for_halt` hands them to `_reconcile_borrowed_folders()` (sequencer.py:1198), and `BorrowedFolderManager.reconcile` reads `lenders_fn=self.borrowed_lenders`. That returns `_borrowed_lenders` (set only at sequencer.py:1699, when a pass adopts a selection), which is empty in a sequencer that never ran. The cached-selection fallback covers projects only.
   - Scenario: restart during a halt, the editor presses tray Pause, the halt is lifted. The projects come back, but a lender this machine borrows from stays paused for as long as Pause holds.
   - Pause is the button that deliberately leaves lane C running, and before this fix nothing paused the lender in that scenario at all.
   - Fix: in the empty-`_last_selection` fallback, also reconcile or release the lenders derived from the cached selection, e.g. `_build_borrowed(cached, ...)` fed to the manager, with its restricted-ignores check intact.

2. `halt_all_sync` writes every folder twice, on the reporter thread, when the folder list cannot be read.
   - `halt_all_sync` first runs `_pause_lane_c_folders(True)`, then `_reassert_halt_pause()` synchronously (app.py:7692).
   - When `get_folders()` fails, `halt_folder_ids_to_repause` returns every id unfiltered (sequencer.py:1146). So every folder `_pause_lane_c_folders` just wrote is PATCHed again.
   - The ledger says the second write per folder happens only for a sequencer double. It also happens with the real lister whenever the list read fails.
   - Probe (real Sequencer, adopted selection s-a/s-b, `get_folders` raising): `app.halt_all_sync('fleet', scope='fleet')` wrote `[('s-a', True), ('s-b', True), ('s-a', True), ('s-b', True)]`.
   - Against a Syncthing that hangs rather than refuses, the fleet halt path (`_apply_fleet_halt` on the reporter thread) grows from N×30 s to N×30 s + 5 s + N×30 s. That is the blocking-on-the-reporter shape round-1 point 3 moved off the startup path.
   - Fix: pass `_reassert_halt_pause` the ids already written, or skip its fallback write when the lister's read failed.

Note, not a defect: `release_for_halt`'s fallback now issues one synchronous `get_ignores` GET per cached folder on whichever thread lifts the halt (the reporter thread for a fleet release). It is bounded, and it is the same verification `_startup_unpause` already runs.

fixes.fix:
Second rework. Both residual defects the round-2 reviewer found were real, and both are fixed.

(1) After a restart, borrowed lender folders were re-paused but never released. release_for_halt's fallback for an empty `_last_selection` now builds the lender map from the cached selection through the new `Sequencer._lenders_from()`, which uses the same `_build_borrowed` validation a pass does; `halt_folder_ids_to_repause` now uses it too. The map is lent to BorrowedFolderManager for that one reconcile through `_halt_release_lenders`. `borrowed_lenders()` falls back to it only while the adopted map is empty, and it is cleared in a `finally`, so it is never adopted. The manager's restricted-.stignore check still decides every unpause, and `_drop_unborrowed` stays inert.

(2) halt_all_sync wrote every folder twice when Syncthing's folder list could not be read. `_pause_lane_c_folders` now takes an optional `attempted` set and records every id it tried to write. halt_all_sync passes that set as `skip` to `_reassert_halt_pause`, which leaves those ids out. When its lister raises, the re-pause returns 0 instead of rewriting everything. A failed write is retried by the next start's off-thread re-pause, not on the reporter thread.

The ledger's Round 2 review note corrects the round-1 claim that the double write happened only with a sequencer double. Companion-only, no wire change.

NEW NEIGHBOUR DEFECT, introduced by the review-round rework: the synthetic give-up record never clears once the machine moves on to a newer build. It is written at upgrade.py:502-507 (version=vX, attempts=MAX_UPGRADE_ATTEMPTS, last_error=crash-looped). The only thing that clears the counters is app.py:6655 `_load_upgrade_state`, and only when record.version == the running VERSION. A successful update writes nothing to the ledger. So in the normal recovery (vX crash-loops, the machine reverts to vX-1, the admin publishes vY and the machine takes it), the machine keeps reporting sync_guard.upgrade = {version: vX, attempts: 8, last_error: "crash-looped"} on vY for ever. That lasts until it happens to fail an attempt at some other version, or runs vX. Probe in the scratchpad (probe1.py): note_reverted_from('0.9.78'), then clear_reverted_from, then CompanionApp._load_upgrade_state with VERSION='0.9.79'. The report still carries version 0.9.78, attempts 8, last_error crash-looped, and tray._upgrade_line returns its warning. What a healthy, updated machine then shows: dashboard alerts._check_upgrade_failed (alerts.py:1774-1793, threshold 8, no version check) fires and tells the admin to "install the build by hand", which is the build that crash-looped. There is also a permanent red [ UPDATE FAILED x8 ] on fleet_grid.html:256 and admin_packages.html:513-514, "an update keeps failing" (health.py:1245), and a permanent Settings WARNING on the editor's machine: settings_window.py:195 -> tray.py:3592-3614 "CCSync could not install the update to v0.9.78 8 times, so it has stopped trying", which is also false, since it did install it. The dashboard-side reverted chip clears itself once running >= reverted (db.py:5371-5381); this record has no such clear. The ledger's OWED items (b)/(c) cover the wording, not this staleness, and the tray/Settings line is not listed at all. Before this rework, a revert followed by a move to vY left nothing stale. Fix, companion-side and with no wire change: in _load_upgrade_state (app.py:6654-6657), also clear the counters when last_error == ERROR_CRASH_LOOPED and the running VERSION is newer than record.version (compare_to_running / version tuple). Keep the crash_looped list, which still gates a rollback push of vX. Optionally, make tray._upgrade_line say "kept crashing and was rolled back" for that code. Add a regression test: revert off 0.9.78, run as 0.9.79, and the report must carry attempts 0 while crash_looped_on('0.9.78') stays true. Residual skew limit, as documented: a 0.9.77 that reverts and then takes vY keeps the stale record until vY (fixed) starts, and with the proposed clear, vY cleans it up on its first start.

Remaining defect, in the finding's own card-dump scenario: file_moves.py:525 takes the snapshot of local files (_files_under) BEFORE the network listing at :535, which can take up to 120 s. When every snapshotted file is on the server, the list of kept files is empty, so apply_move skips the per-file path (:721) and moves the WHOLE directory into .ccsync-trash at :736 (src.replace(trash)). A file that landed in the folder during the listing window was never checked against the server and goes to the trash with the folder. Lane A never walks the trash, and prune_trash deletes it after 14 days.

I reproduced this in a scratch probe. The server_files stub writes Card_07/A002.mov into the folder, then returns only A001.mov. Result: (True, 'trashed locally, destination not synced here'), and A002.mov is in .ccsync-trash/<stamp>/Projects/2026/X/Card_07/. On macOS the rename also succeeds under a Finder copy that is still running, and that copy keeps writing into the trash. On Windows, an open handle makes the rename fail, but a file finished between the snapshot and the rename is lost. Suggested fix: when a folder was triaged against a listing, trash it file by file through _apply_4b_partial even when nothing is kept, and remove the emptied tree only with rmdir. Or re-scan after the listing and keep any file missing from the first snapshot.

Minor note: rclone lsf (timeout 120 s) runs on the reporter thread once per 4b folder move per attempt, one move after another. On a hung SFTP, several folder moves in one reply stall the report by N x 120 s. This is bounded and on the retry schedule, so it is not blocking. The live rclone lsf path has also still not run against the NAS, which the ledger already lists as owed.

fixes.fix: Round 2 (2026-09-25). Every section 4b FOLDER now goes through _apply_4b_partial file by file, even when nothing is kept. The whole-folder src.replace(trash) is now used only for single files. _apply_4b_partial (1) moves only the files that were snapshotted AND matched the listing, and re-stats each one first: a file whose size changed since the snapshot is kept. (2) Re-scans the folder after the moves and keeps anything still in it, including files that landed during the up-to-120 s listing. (3) Removes only the directories it left empty, with rmdir deepest-first, never rmtree. When nothing is kept, the answer is unchanged (DETAIL_NOT_SYNCED_HERE, paths=None), so nothing changes on the wire and app.py is untouched. _split_folder_for_4b now returns (path, rel, size). docs/FILE_MOVES.md section 3 and docs/HAND_MOVES_ON_THE_SERVER.md 4b now describe this. Round-1 items are resolved in the code, not only in the ledger. (a) NAS half: ytdl/web/ytdlweb/vendor/downloader.py:434-491 now moves the original to `<stem>.source.editready<ext>` before the ffmpeg `-i`. The outcomes are correct: unstage on ffmpeg failure, a failed guess, FileNotFoundError or any other exception, then remove the staged file and `_swap_in(tmp, final, final)` on success. `_swap_in`'s same=True path still moves a held file at `final` aside. worker._INTERMEDIATE_STEM (worker.py:902) makes the staged name sweepable, `_landed_file` refuses it, and ytsearch._ID_RE/_ARTIFACT_EXT_RE do not count it as a finished clip. The name spelling is pinned against the companion's in server/tests/test_cross_component.py:1203-1207. (b) Stop during the probe: ytdl_executor.py:2521-2535 moves the unchecked download onto the staged name so `_cleanup_current` -> clear_partials sweeps it. (c) The crash-abandoned residual is disclosed and accepted.

Tests I ran. On the fix: companion 352 passed (test_ytdl_executor, test_youtube_import, test_rclone_filters, test_bug_hunt_2026_09_24_comp_media); ytdl/web 269 passed; server test_cross_component 70 passed. Against HEAD, in scratch copies with only a staged_source_name helper appended: the three companion regressions fail on the defect itself, all with `['Some Channe...aaaaaaa].mp4'] == []` (long conversion, stop mid-conversion, and stop during the probe, which also fails on HEAD). Both ytdl/web parametrised cases fail with `{'during': ['...[aaaaaaaaaaa].mp4'], 'landed': '...'} != {'during': [], 'landed': None}`. No wire change, so no skew risk between companion 0.9.77 and dashboard 0.7.57 in either direction. None of the new code runs on a startup or reporter thread.

New neighbour defect the fix introduces. companion/src/ccsync_companion/proxy_scan.py:415-434 (scan_project) picks candidates by VIDEO_EXTS and a 120 s mtime settle only. It never applies lane A's YTDL_WORK_EXCLUDE_RULES or the `.editready` stem rule, so the staged source is queued for a proxy. Probe: scan_project over `Youtube/<term>/Some Channel - A clip [aaaaaaaaaaa].source.editready.webm` aged 600 s returned it as a `preview` candidate (missing=1). Its expected proxy is `Proxy/<title> [id].source.editready.mp4`. On HEAD the same scan proxied the original under its deliverable stem, so `Proxy/<title> [id].mp4` also covered the converted final. With the fix, the base rig's generator will now do the following for any NAS conversion that outlasts 120 s plus a 900 s scan tick (4K/1440p VP9, the case this fix targets):
- Encode a 540p preview of the staged file and publish `Youtube/<term>/Proxy/<title> [id].source.editready.mp4`. That path is an orphan with no original. Lane B's `+ **/Proxy/**` (rclone_lane.py:723-735, which has no editready rule) carries it to every editor with the project ticked, and nothing ever removes it.
- Encode the converted final a second time.
- If the worker's os.remove(staged) wins the race, record an encode failure against a path that will never come back.
An editor machine running proxy_gen gets the same local orphan. Fix: have proxy_scan skip the ytdl work names, either with rclone_lane.path_matches_lane_a_filter / YTDL_WORK_EXCLUDE_RES or with the `.editready|.original|.fNNN|.temp` stem rule, consistent with its own comment "if a lane wouldn't carry it, its absence downstream is not a proxy gap". Add a test with a staged `.source.editready.webm`.

Minor, not blocking: ytdl_executor.py:2615-2621. On a Windows editor, a successful conversion whose staged original is still open elsewhere (the local proxy generator above, AV, or the Explorer thumbnailer) fails `os.remove(staged)`, and the log says "it is swept on the next attempt". A clip that succeeded has no next attempt on this machine (clear_partials runs only on a stop or on a new attempt at that id). So a full-size VP9 copy is left permanently from the ordinary success path, not only from a crash. It is excluded from every lane, so the cost is local disk. Either the log should say so, or the file should be retried from clear_aside_originals-style housekeeping.

fixes.fix: Round 2 rework, fixing both of the reviewer's points. (1) The proxy scanner was queuing the staged source for a proxy. Fixed in companion/src/ccsync_companion/proxy_scan.py: scan_project now skips every basename that matches rclone_lane.YTDL_WORK_EXCLUDE_RES. That is the compiled form of lane A's own YTDL_WORK_EXCLUDE_RULES, so the scanner cannot drift from the lanes. This means `<title> [id].source.editready.<ext>` no longer produces an orphan `Proxy/<title> [id].source.editready.mp4` that lane B would carry to every editor, and the converted final is no longer encoded twice. The skip also covers .editready, .original, .fNNN and .temp files. (2) On the success path, a staged original that is still held could stay on disk silently. Fixed in companion/src/ccsync_companion/ytdl_executor.py with a new DownloadJob._remove_staged. It makes 4 tries 0.5 s apart through deps.sleep. If the file is still held after that: a WARNING says nothing will retry it and how many bytes stay; the clip row's note names the file and its size and says it syncs nowhere and can be deleted (no em dash). The misleading 'swept on the next attempt' log is gone. No wire change. The ledger note 'Round 2 review' is under bug-comp-ytdl-1 in docs/bug-hunt-2026-09-24/ledger/comp-media.md.

Problems remaining in the rewritten runbook:
(A) Step 2 (docs/RELEASE.md:695-701) tells the operator to add the new public key to DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS 'on this studio's dashboard'. On pathway A that setting is undone by every ship. tools/load_secrets.ps1:156-161 (which ship.ps1:339 tells the operator to dot-source) SETS env:DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS to release.key's public half ONLY. server/install_dashboard_app.py:2623 then writes that env into the container on ship.cmd's dashboard deploy step. So during steps 1-2 each ship redeploys the studio dashboard trusting the old key only. After the step 3 switch, load_secrets derives the NEW key only, so the studio dashboard stops trusting the old key: records signed by it, the vendor channel still signed by it, and OTA code trees checked by dashboard/deploy/select_code_root.py:237-240. That is the exact state step 2 exists to prevent. The runbook needs a line for the rotation window: set $env:DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS to 'old,new' after load_secrets. Or load_secrets should keep a second key. The fix never mentions load_secrets.
(B) Step 3's key switch (docs/RELEASE.md:702-710) moves only the files on this rig. tools/release_macos.sh:811-812 and build_onboard_macos.sh:508-510 sign Mac builds with a hand-copied ~/.ccsync-release/release.key on the Mac, and that path has no REL-7 check at all. A Mac that keeps the old key keeps signing with it past the switch. After the later 'drop the old key' release, those Mac builds are refused by every Mac on the drop build, and nothing warns. The runbook should say to replace or retire the Mac's copy at step 3. Lower severity: before the DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS drop, the dashboard still accepts those builds, and after the drop it refuses them loudly.
(C) Minor: test_step3_says_pathway_a_needs_the_override_once_and_when (tools/tests/test_bug_hunt_2026_09_24_webapps_ops.py:193-222) only models the ps1 as one equality on a record it wrote itself. It mostly pins doc strings, so it would not catch the ps1 comparison changing.

fixes.fix: Round 2 review, second rework. (A) The rotation now keeps both keys trusted on the studio dashboard. load_secrets.ps1 used to set DASH_RELEASE_PUBKEYS to release.key's public half only, and ship.cmd's dashboard deploy writes that value into the container, so every ship during a rotation took one key away. tools/release_key.py has a new `trusted` subcommand. It prints release.key's public half, then the halves of release-next.key and release.key.superseded whenever they sit beside it. An unreadable one refuses; it is never skipped. load_secrets.ps1 now calls `trusted --quiet` and reports 'N keys: a key rotation is under way'. docs/RELEASE.md changes: step 2 is split into this studio's dashboard (reload load_secrets, never hand-set, on pathway B run ship.cmd -DashboardOnly once) and customer dashboards (add the key by hand). Step 3 keeps release.key.superseded on the rig until step 4. A new step 4 drops the old key: bake without --add in a later release, then move release.key.superseded off the rig, reload and ship. (B) Step 3 gains a Mac bullet. release_macos.sh and build_onboard_macos.sh sign with the Mac's hand-copied ~/.ccsync-release/release.key and have no REL-7 check. Replace that file at the switch and confirm `python3 tools/release_key.py pubkey` prints the NEW id there. The bullet also says what a stale Mac key costs. (C) The step-3 test now runs the ps1's own Get-PubkeyId and Test-SigningKeyTheFleetTrusts under PowerShell, cut from installer/build_editor_package.ps1, with only Invoke-RestMethod (fed the real feed record) and the console helpers stubbed. The overlap build passes. The first new-key build exits 1 with WILL REFUSE and names the old key id. The override lets it through. Any change to the ps1 comparison now turns the test red.
